questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have a personal relationship with Germany, and the university I chose had courses taught in English which was essential for me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The mobility online system was quite difficult to navigate in, but the websites of my home university and exchange university was helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a buddy from the buddy program at University of Mannheim, who helped me in the beginning.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: We were told to be available one full week for introduction purposes, however there was less introduction from the university than expected.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through Studierendenwerk Mannheim, which is an organization connected to the university, who provides the housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There were no actual on-campus housing, so it's the same for everyone.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I recommend living in the quadrate close to Jungbusch, which is close to the uni and filled with restaurants, bars and young people.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to send an email to the faculty in order to apply for courses, by prioritizing them. There was a list specifically for exchange students with the relevant ECTS-credits.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange coordinator from the university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't hesitate to contact your coordinator if you have any questions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was fit for master courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In most classes, there was a lot of talking/presentation by the teacher and no student involvement, which is very different from UCPH. It made the lectures very long and hard to take part in. I did however get used to it over time. But in one of my classes it was the opposite, and the teacher was very good at creating a safe teaching environment where students would and could participate.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: International business transactions, international sale of goods, introduction to German constitutional law, international criminal law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International business transactions. The teacher was excellent, and the course was very difficult but interesting. Also a very nice experience at the examination.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The washing and drying at the student housing was quite expensive, but food was a lot less expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Germans are way more out-going than Danish people, which was helpful in the adjustment proces.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Use the many ESN-Visum events to meet both local and exchange students - and your buddy.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open, go on trips (use the trains), be patient with the paper work.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and cultures, getting to experience law from a different point of view, and taking courses not available at UCPH.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adapting to the language and feeling homesick.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
